channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Politico Europe] Poland arrests second man over threats to Prime Minister Tusk
item.description: The 46-year-old suspect allegedly posted messages calling for the killing of Donald Tusk on Facebook and TikTok.

item.title: [Financial Times] How not to revive Europe’s auto industry
item.description: The electric vehicle market shows how legacy EU companies continue to fail when it comes to countering Chinese competition

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen pledges more cash for Egypt and Libya regimes to keep Sudanese genocide victims out of Europe
item.description: They fled genocide in Sudan to find persecution in Egypt so they moved on to Libya, but von der Leyen aims to pay Cairo and Tripoli to keep Sudanese refugees out of Fortress EU.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Lights, bells and liability: Europe’s privacy regulators crack down on smart glasses
item.description: Smart glasses firms could be forced to build in flashing lights, audio alerts to abide by EU privacy law.

item.title: [Financial Times] White House asks US envoy to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign
item.description: Donald Trump had said he was considering firing the ambassador after reports claiming she accepted improper gifts

item.title: [Financial Times] Chip stocks slide in wake of ‘casino’ comment by Broadcom boss
item.description: Declines for Samsung and SK Hynix drag Kospi sharply lower as investors fret over scale of AI investment

item.title: [Politico Europe] Bruno Retailleau temporise sur la relance du nucléaire
item.description: Le candidat LR à l’élection présidentielle préfère les réacteurs de quatrième génération, a-t-il déclaré au sommet pour la compétitivité de POLITICO.

item.title: [EU Observer] Burnham to prioritise trade and migration at UK-EU summit, after accusing Russia of meddling in Brexit referendum
item.description: The UK-EU "status quo is not good enough for Britain", claimed the British prime minister after accusing Russia of meddling in the Brexit referendum.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Il faut “absolument” réduire la contribution française au budget de l’UE, selon Bruno Retailleau
item.description: Le président des Républicains assure rester pour autant "pro-européen".

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine had ‘no warning’ of latest Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv
item.description: Zelenskyy said intelligence sharing is "precisely what helps prevent people from being killed."

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump either ‘a useful idiot’ or purposefully weakening Europe, says MEP Glucksmann
item.description: Fresh off his primary win, the French presidential candidate showcased his pro-EU and pro-Kyiv stances at POLITICO’s Competitiveness Summit in Paris.

item.title: [EU Observer] Socialist MEPs urge von der Leyen to cap methane-rules delay at one year, or withdraw it
item.description: In a letter sent on Monday to commission president von der Leyen, five centre-left MEPs said any postponement must be “strictly limited to a single year.”

item.title: [Politico Europe] Lagarde’s book plug raises questions about ECB ethics standards
item.description: The ECB president strongly encouraged reporters to buy her memoir, Lady First, during a press conference last month.

item.title: [Politico Europe] MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
item.description: MI5 has launched the AI Threat Assessment Centre to help Britain respond to state threats, terrorism and bioweapons.

item.title: [Financial Times] Bulgaria suggests Russia behind ship attack that left 11 sailors missing
item.description: Strike on cargo ship marks latest escalation in Russia-Ukraine war in the Black Sea

item.title: [Financial Times] Zelenskyy says Kyiv’s partners failed to warn of ballistic missile attack
item.description: The Ukrainian leader stops short of linking intelligence gap to Trump administration’s threats to withdraw US support

item.title: [DW] Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
item.description: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move; critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.

item.title: [Financial Times] Cyber attack on French supermarket fridges raises alarm over food security
item.description: Some stores reported fridge temperatures as high as 80°C, melting equipment and destroying food

item.title: [Politico Europe] Backtracking on green energy contracts would be a mistake, warns Engie boss
item.description: Subsidies for clean energy projects are key for France's energy sovereignty, says Engie CEO Catherine MacGregor.

item.title: [Politico Europe] France’s Philippe says Le Pen’s EU proposals would ‘crack open’ bloc
item.description: The center-right candidate said at a POLITICO event that his far-right rival was selling the French 'fantasy' plans on the economy.

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic warns rogue AI agents may ‘self-replicate’ to hijack ovens
item.description: Claude maker suggests models could act as ‘worms’ to spread across smart home appliances such as lawnmowers and TVs in future cyber security threat

item.title: [Financial Times] How US coal mined ties to Trump — and got much of its ‘wish list’
item.description: A CEO golfs with Trump’s son as an industry once shut out of Washington turns access into policy

item.title: [Financial Times] Bumper equities trading helps Goldman overcome Wall Street’s fixed income woes
item.description: Performance of stock traders helps Goldman report 30 per cent rise in third-quarter net income

item.title: [EU Observer] Who ordered the strike that killed my friend and maimed me? The EU must demand answers from Israel
item.description: I survived an Israeli strike on 13 October 2023 with one leg missing, while my friend and colleague Issam was killed. Yet three years later, no one has been held accountable. I am asking the EU to turn its commitments to protecting journalists into concrete action: demand answers from Israel and use its leverage to ensure that those responsible face justice.

item.title: [DW] Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
item.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Could the EU shield the ICC from US sanctions?
item.description: The United States has imposed new sanctions on the International Criminal Court, this time targeting the institution itself. The EU, while supportive of the ICC, does little to counter the sanctions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Poll shows public revulsion on caged hens ahead of EU-ban deadline
item.description: In a poll of 25,080 adults across 25 EU member states, 75 percent of Europeans indicated support for a hen-cage ban by 2035.

item.title: [DW] What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
item.description: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

item.title: [Financial Times] Why Trump is going for Zelenskyy’s jugular
item.description: No matter how much America’s allies urge the president to back Ukraine, he cannot forgive its leader for showing up his dealmaking impotence

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s skills passport is missing a page, EMPASS wants to add it
item.description: Employers are reporting skills bottlenecks because CVs and qualifications often fail to capture skills they are looking for. Europe needs bridges between education and employment.

item.title: [DW] EU pulls sponsorship from Disinfo2026 event in Lithuania
item.description: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania all pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. Amid reports of US pressure, the EU said it was "uncomfortable with the framing" of some panels.

item.title: [DW] Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
item.description: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Bulgaria has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

item.title: [DW] Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
item.description: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

item.title: [DW] Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.

item.title: [DW] Georgia's surrogacy industry is booming, but at what cost?
item.description: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

item.title: [EU Observer] France, Greece, and Netherlands see steep fall in crisis-resilience, study finds
item.description: With one in five adults worldwide hit by disasters in the past five years, millions of people in Greece and France could be dangerously exposed when the next natural or man-made crisis strikes.

item.title: [DW] UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.

item.title: [DW] Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
item.description: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs don’t have to meekly accept an EU budget deal, but will they go to war over €141bn in cuts?
item.description: MEPs and the champions of EU integration point to the parliament's co-decision powers as proof of the institution's importance. But will MEPs dare use those powers in a budget fight with governments?

item.title: [Financial Times] Zuckerberg says Meta has reached AI ‘frontier’
item.description: FT interview: tech billionaire touts release of new Muse Wonder model after vast spending to challenge rivals in AI race

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Spanish socialist MEP sees no other leader than Sánchez, as housing and immigration dominate snap election
item.description: Some 23 percent of Spain’s working population were immigrants, who were “paying taxes and [contributing to] pensions for everyone," said the MEP, ahead of a snap election dominated by its housing crisis and the Ceuta migrant crisis.

item.title: [EU Observer] Forged news of military conscripts in Kaliningrad had hallmarks of a Western counter-attack in Putin’s info wars
item.description: Western spymasters may finally be testing Kremlin-style information tricks on Russian soil to rattle Putin’s war regime.

item.title: [EU Observer] Tanks vs. drones battle exposes lie in Russia’s map of territorial gains, as Ukraine once again bombs Yandex data centres (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,691)
item.description: Drones are now deciding who survives on the battlefield — and even which side's maps or propaganda can still be believed.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Made in Europe’ wind, solar, and nuclear power can protect us from future energy shocks
item.description: Brussels is betting on a rapid build-out of homegrown renewables and nuclear to shield households and industry from the next energy shock.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Should we be worried about Europe’s level of gas reserves?
item.description: European gas storage levels are unusually low for this time of year, reaching their lowest autumn level since 2011. With Russian gas imports set to end in 2027, could Europe face a tougher challenge in the months ahead?

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Ex-Bosnia envoy sees no risk of renewed violence, but the fractured country’s EU dream is rotting away
item.description: As one of Dayton’s former guardians, Schmidt fears less instability than a quiet collapse of trust, as youth reject segregated schools, politicians glorify war criminals, and Europe fails to turn Bosnia’s pro-EU mood into real opportunities.

item.title: [DW] Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
item.description: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

item.title: [DW] Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
item.description: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

item.title: [DW] Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
item.description: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia-Herzegovina will soon have a new grand mufti
item.description: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

item.title: [DW] Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?
